question: Unto whom does the apostle John specifically address his third canonical epistle, designating him with intimate pastoral affection?
opt1: The elder unto the wellbeloved Gaius, whom I love in the truth
opt2: The elder unto the faithful bishop Timothy, my beloved son in the faith
opt3: The elder unto Philemon our dearly beloved, and fellowlabourer in Colosse
opt4: The elder unto Titus, mine own son after the common faith in Crete
correct: The elder unto the wellbeloved Gaius, whom I love in the truth
explanation: John addresses his personal pastoral letter to his beloved friend Gaius, emphasizing that their relationship is established firmly upon the bedrock of divine truth. 3 John 1:1 (KJV) - "The elder unto the wellbeloved Gaius, whom I love in the truth."

question: What comprehensive pastoral blessing does John pronounce upon Gaius regarding his physical health and financial welfare in comparison to his soul?
opt1: Beloved, I pray that thou mayest attain municipal magistracies and rule over secular courts
opt2: Beloved, I wish above all things that thou mayest prosper and be in health, even as thy soul prospereth
opt3: Beloved, I desire that thou mayest withdraw into solitary ascetic fasting away from all trade
opt4: Beloved, I entreat that thou mayest construct monumental stone basilicas across Asia
correct: Beloved, I wish above all things that thou mayest prosper and be in health, even as thy soul prospereth
explanation: John expresses a balanced pastoral desire for Gaius's physical health and temporal prosperity to mirror his already thriving spiritual condition. 3 John 1:2 (KJV) - "Beloved, I wish above all things that thou mayest prosper and be in health, even as thy soul prospereth."

question: What does the apostle John declare to be his greatest source of joy concerning his spiritual children in the faith?
opt1: To hear that they have amassed immense fortunes through Mediterranean maritime commerce
opt2: To hear that they have defeated pagan philosophers in public oratorical debates
opt3: I have no greater joy than to hear that my children walk in truth
opt4: To hear that their names are recorded on royal monuments erected by Roman proconsuls
correct: I have no greater joy than to hear that my children walk in truth
explanation: Nothing brings greater pastoral fulfillment to the apostle than receiving credible reports from brethren that his spiritual children are consistently living out divine truth. 3 John 1:3-4 (KJV) - "For I rejoiced greatly, when the brethren came and testified of the truth that is in thee, even as thou walkest in the truth. I have no greater joy than to hear that my children walk in truth."

question: What faithful service performed by Gaius was publicly testified before the assembly by travelling Christian ministers?
opt1: Thou hast funded the construction of armed fortresses to defend the assembly from Roman soldiers
opt2: Thou hast composed elaborate philosophical commentaries reconciling the gospel with Stoic logic
opt3: Thou hast enforced strict ceremonial fasts and dietary abstinences upon all visiting pilgrims
opt4: Thou doest faithfully whatsoever thou doest to the brethren, and to strangers; which have borne witness of thy charity before the church
correct: Thou doest faithfully whatsoever thou doest to the brethren, and to strangers; which have borne witness of thy charity before the church
explanation: Gaius earned high commendation for his generous, faithful hospitality toward traveling evangelists and missionary strangers, who recounted his charity before the church. 3 John 1:5-6 (KJV) - "Beloved, thou doest faithfully whatsoever thou doest to the brethren, and to strangers; Which have borne witness of thy charity before the church: whom if thou bring forward on their journey after a godly sort, thou shalt do well:"

question: For whose sake did these itinerant evangelists go forth, and why are local believers obligated to support them?
opt1: Because that for his name's sake they went forth, taking nothing of the Gentiles. We therefore ought to receive such, that we might be fellowhelpers to the truth
opt2: Because for secular wages they went forth, collecting tithes from Roman municipal treasuries
opt3: Because for personal fame they went forth, seeking honorary citizenship from provincial governors
opt4: Because for commercial gain they went forth, selling sacred relics and certificates to pagan merchants
correct: Because that for his name's sake they went forth, taking nothing of the Gentiles. We therefore ought to receive such, that we might be fellowhelpers to the truth
explanation: Missionaries went forth solely for the honor of Christ's name, deliberately refusing financial support from pagan Gentiles, making church hospitality an essential partnership in gospel truth. 3 John 1:7-8 (KJV) - "Because that for his name's sake they went forth, taking nothing of the Gentiles. We therefore ought to receive such, that we might be fellowhelpers to the truth."

question: How does John describe the tyrannical pride and divisive conduct of Diotrephes within the local congregation?
opt1: Diotrephes, who secretly adopted the ascetic doctrines of the Essenes and withdrew into the desert
opt2: Diotrephes, who loveth to have the preeminence among them, receiveth us not
opt3: Diotrephes, who bribed the Roman garrison commander to shut down the local synagogue
opt4: Diotrephes, who refused to observe the weekly sabbath according to the custom of the Jews
correct: Diotrephes, who loveth to have the preeminence among them, receiveth us not
explanation: Diotrephes represents authoritarian self-exaltation in church leadership, craving personal dominance (preeminence) and obstinately rejecting apostolic authority. 3 John 1:9 (KJV) - "I wrote unto the church: but Diotrephes, who loveth to have the preeminence among them, receiveth us not."

question: What four abusive and dictatorial deeds of Diotrephes does John promise to bring to remembrance when he arrives in person?
opt1: Embezzling community funds, selling church furniture, desecrating scriptures, and burning hymn scrolls
opt2: Imposing heavy financial tithes, ordaining unqualified novices, practicing astrology, and neglecting the sick
opt3: Prating against us with malicious words: neither doth he himself receive the brethren, and forbiddeth them that would, and casteth them out of the church
opt4: Appealing to Caesar, bribing municipal magistrates, forming armed factions, and closing the harbor
correct: Prating against us with malicious words: neither doth he himself receive the brethren, and forbiddeth them that would, and casteth them out of the church
explanation: John exposes Diotrephes's fourfold misconduct: slandering apostles with malicious talk, refusing hospitality to visiting missionaries, intimidating hospitable saints, and excommunicating generous believers. 3 John 1:10 (KJV) - "Wherefore, if I come, I will remember his deeds which he doeth, prating against us with malicious words: and not content therewith, neither doth he himself receive the brethren, and forbiddeth them that would, and casteth them out of the church."

question: What fundamental moral maxim does John set before Gaius to distinguish those who belong to God from those who do not?
opt1: Beloved, follow the customs of the majority, for popular consensus determines righteous conduct
opt2: Beloved, seek after outward ceremonial purity, for ritual washings conceal secret moral faults
opt3: Beloved, submit to autocratic leaders, for unquestioned subservience secures divine blessing
opt4: Beloved, follow not that which is evil, but that which is good. He that doeth good is of God: but he that doeth evil hath not seen God
correct: Beloved, follow not that which is evil, but that which is good. He that doeth good is of God: but he that doeth evil hath not seen God
explanation: One's habitual moral conduct reveals one's spiritual origin: practicing goodness reflects birth from God, whereas practicing evil demonstrates spiritual blindness to God. 3 John 1:11 (KJV) - "Beloved, follow not that which is evil, but that which is good. He that doeth good is of God: but he that doeth evil hath not seen God."

question: What threefold authoritative testimony does John present to commend Demetrius as a godly model for the church?
opt1: Demetrius hath good report of all men, and of the truth itself: yea, and we also bear record; and ye know that our record is true
opt2: Demetrius hath received honorary civic laurels, inherited vast estates, and attained Roman citizenship
opt3: Demetrius hath memorized the entire Torah, observed all fasts, and offered costly sacrifices in Jerusalem
opt4: Demetrius hath written eloquent rhetorical orations, mastered Greek philosophy, and governed municipal forums
correct: Demetrius hath good report of all men, and of the truth itself: yea, and we also bear record; and ye know that our record is true
explanation: In sharp contrast to Diotrephes, Demetrius possesses an unassailable threefold endorsement: universal public reputation, alignment with biblical truth, and apostolic witness. 3 John 1:12 (KJV) - "Demetrius hath good report of all men, and of the truth itself: yea, and we also bear record; and ye know that our record is true."

question: How does the apostle John conclude his third epistle regarding written communication and personal greetings?
opt1: I have concluded all instructions, and command thee to read this letter in every synagogue throughout Asia. Farewell. Amen
opt2: I had many things to write, but I will not with ink and pen write unto thee: but I trust I shall shortly see thee, and we shall speak face to face. Peace be to thee. Our friends salute thee. Greet the friends by name
opt3: I must depart immediately for the imperial capital to plead my case before Caesar. Pray for my release. Amen
opt4: I urge thee to sell all thy possessions and join the elders in the wilderness. Grace be multiplied unto all. Amen
correct: I had many things to write, but I will not with ink and pen write unto thee: but I trust I shall shortly see thee, and we shall speak face to face. Peace be to thee. Our friends salute thee. Greet the friends by name
explanation: John reserves further instruction for an imminent face-to-face visit, concluding with a benediction of peace and an intimate pastoral command to greet local Christian friends individually by name. 3 John 1:13-14 (KJV) - "I had many things to write, but I will not with ink and pen write unto thee: But I trust I shall shortly see thee, and we shall speak face to face. Peace be to thee. Our friends salute thee. Greet the friends by name."
